nodes.text: FAST · ON-DEVICE AI This file is a summary of the Constitution of the United States , covering its adoption in 1787 and outlining key provisions regarding the federal government's structure, powers, and specific rules. Here are the main points from the document: • [2] The Constitution establishes a federal system where Congress holds legislative power, with the House of Representatives elected every two years by direct election and Senators serving six-year terms appointed by state legislatures [1]. • [4] A bill cannot be signed into law or vetoed; it must pass both houses before being presented to the President, who may sign it or return objections requiring a two-thirds vote in each house [2]. • [3] The President serves four-year terms and holds office as Commander in Chief of the Army, Navy, and Militia. No state can levy duties on imports or exports without Congress's consent, with revenue from such taxes dedicated solely to the federal Treasury [1][3]. • [2] The Constitution mandates uniformity of taxes across all states while prohibiting duties on exported goods and grants Congress power over taxation and commerce [2]. • [4] Treason is defined as levying war, adhering to enemies, or aiding them, requiring two witnesses for conviction. It also guarantees every state a republican form of government and protection against invasion and domestic violence upon application by the legislature or executive [3][4]. • [1] New states may only be admitted with Congress's consent, prohibiting forming new states from joining existing ones without legislative and congressional approval [4].
